models.summary: Health is a point (EP, SI) on a nine-box McKinsey matrix and a distance d to (1,1). Twenty indicators in four dimensions, drawn from the OECD INES framework with an added context dimension. Entropy weights inside each dimension; AHP weights across the four dimensions, given as (0.4018, 0.1374, 0.2547, 0.2062). SI is the output-input ratio. Box edges come from K-means: EP at 0.30 and 0.60, SI at 0.14 and 0.41. On five countries the UK lands in the best box, d = 0.4803, and Italy in the bottom middle, d = 1.0785, which makes Italy the case.
models.purpose: Score any country's higher education twice, once for level and once for balance, and turn the pair into one distance.
objectives: Compress twenty indicators into a level, a balance, and a distance to the ideal corner.

equation_status.note: Equations (1)-(9) are glyph-garbled. Reconstructed as standard entropy weighting, a weighted sum, a ratio and a Euclidean distance. The weight table and the five country scores are readable.

details: 49 countries, twenty years, from World Bank, UIS and ILOSTAT. Missing values filled by mean, by regression on the year, or by the cross-country mean.
Benefit, cost and interval attributes normalized differently. STEM judged an interval attribute on [16.7, 32] after its ranking failed to match the ranking by top universities.

parameter_estimation.method: Entropy weights within each dimension, AHP across dimensions, K-means for the two thresholds on each axis.

algorithm.description: Normalize, weight by entropy inside each dimension, weight the dimensions by AHP, form the ratio, cluster to get box edges, measure distance to (1,1).
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not applicable. Closed computation plus one clustering.

details: UK d = 0.4803 in the best box. US 0.6397, Czech Republic 0.9806, Italy 1.0785, Thailand 1.1558. Switzerland is tabulated but not discussed.
identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The distance orders the five countries and the box locates Italy's weakness: medium level, low balance. Both numbers are needed; either alone would hide the shape.

constraints: Sample is the richer countries, then applied to all.
SI uses only output over input, ignoring context and participation.
strengths: The borrowed framework is named and then corrected in two stated ways.
One attribute, STEM, is tested against a proxy instead of asserted.
limitations: The entropy sentence contradicts the entropy formula.
The country chosen to represent the world is chosen for being developed, which the model then confirms.
assumptions: No major crisis in the coming decades.
Rich countries represent world higher education.
A country behaves like a business unit.
A limited indicator set can reflect health fully.

models.summary: Two futures for Italy over 2021-2032. Without policy, each indicator is forecast by AR, ARMA or ARIMA in SPSS 24, and SI falls even as EP rises. With policy, five indicators are pushed on a four-phase timetable and the correlated ones move through fitted regressions, one of which has p = 1.842e-8. Other countries are held fixed so Italy's score measures Italy. The policy path ends 0.28 closer to (1,1). A mid-course dip in SI is read as slow absorption of new spending.
models.purpose: Show the policy path beats the untouched path, and explain the one place it temporarily does not.
objectives: Compare twelve years of health with and without the five policies.

details: Italy, annual indicators 2000-2019. Compulsory schooling years held constant.
Other countries frozen, because the score is relative. Policy shocks are phased: 2021-23, 2024-26, 2027-29, 2030-32.
Twelve-year window, no stated steady state.

parameter_estimation.method: Per-indicator model selection in SPSS 24. Regressions kept when significance is high and fit is good. Only one equation's tests are printed.

algorithm.description: Forecast each series, apply the phased policy shocks, propagate them through the regressions, rescore both paths on the frozen world.
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Significance at 0.05 and overall F test. No forecast error is printed.

details: Policy path ends 0.28 closer to (1,1). EP enters the top band; SI approaches but does not cross 0.41. Disturbed d in 2020 is 0.9919 against 0.9909.
identifiability_feasibility.analysis: The comparison is the result. The no-policy path getting worse, because SI collapses, does more work than the policy path getting better.

constraints: Policy effects are stipulated percentages, not estimated.
One printed regression stands for several.
validation_refs: Figure 9 two paths on the matrix
strengths: The counterfactual is computed, not asserted.
The mid-course dip in SI is explained instead of smoothed over.
limitations: Policy magnitudes, 8 percent, 5 percent, 3 percent, are chosen, not derived.
Forecast accuracy is shown for four series only.
missing_details: Orders and errors for the indicators not plotted.
assumptions: Relative ranking with a frozen world still measures progress.
